interfaces.name: PositiveDefiniteTreeLattice.rootedEdgeClassification
interfaces.note: Consumer anchor: Main.RootedEstimates::treePairingRootedChildDecomposition@1. For finite decidable V, G : SimpleGraph V, hG : G.IsTree, root rho, and an ambient adjacency G.Adj u v, classify the unordered edge {u,v} disjointly as either the root-child case (one endpoint is rho and the other is c ∈ rootedChildren G hG rho rho) or an internal case indexed by a unique c ∈ rootedChildren G hG rho rho with u and v represented in rootedChildComponent G rho c and adjacent in that component graph. The capability must provide the directions/uniqueness needed to partition the global adjacency Finset sum and transport endpoints back to V. It must use the existing rootedChildren, rootedChildComponent, and rootedChildRoot representation, assume no weights or admissibility, and not mention treePairing or Main.RootedEstimates.
interfaces.summary: Every edge of a finite rooted tree is either a root-child edge or lies internally in one unique root-child component.

interfaces.name: PositiveDefiniteTreeLattice.rootedChildCount_add_one_eq_degree
interfaces.note: Consumer anchor: Main.IrreducibleVertex::rootedChildComponent_childCount_add_one_eq_degree@1. For {V} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V], G : SimpleGraph V with decidable adjacency, hG : G.IsTree, root ρ and vertex x with hx : x ≠ ρ, prove exactly rootedChildCount G hG ρ x + 1 = G.degree x (or the symmetric equality). Use the current rootedChildren/rootedChildCount definitions. A predecessor/neighborFinset partition may be a helper, but the public capability must require no weights, admissibility, components, or consumer-specific data and must not strengthen hx. This result is applied after rootedChildCount_rootedChildComponent in the retained private consumer.
interfaces.summary: Every nonroot vertex of a finite rooted tree has degree equal to its rooted child count plus one.
